title: manifest
description: What one task execution was going to be given, written before its command runs. It therefore holds only what is known beforehand: anything a run learns by finishing is not in here, because the manifest was closed before there was anything to learn.

task.description: The task this execution belongs to.

ordinal.description: This execution's index within the task.

command.description: The command line as executed, after substitution.

variables.description: Every value exposed as a template variable for this execution, whether or not the command used it, with the layer each came from. A reader sees what the task was given and not only what its command became, which matters where a variable was available and went unused, and where a definition overrode what the jig shipped.

value.description: What the placeholder stood for. A list only where the variable is itself a list of paths.

from.description: Which layer supplied it: a location or path variable bolt reserves, the jig's own definitions block, or the definitions file named on the invocation. The same key means different things depending on which won, and the command line alone does not say.

selection.description: What the task was offered and what it was kept from seeing. Present for a task that consumes paths.

matched.description: The whole matched list, repeated in every execution of a per-path task, because one path alone loses the context of what the task was offered.
